name: in_flight_logic_should_not_sabotage_concurrent_changes
rationale: A reference peer commits another change while its previous message is awaiting acknowledgement.

name: triangle_changes_arrive_via_two_paths
rationale: Three peers relay concurrent changes through native and reference engines and converge to identical heads.

name: generate_sync_message_twice_does_nothing
rationale: A second generation attempt while a message is in flight returns no message.

name: handle_repeated_out_of_order_changes
rationale: Dependent changes are applied child-first in one batch, separately, and repeatedly.

name: splicing_into_multibyte_characters
rationale: UTF-16 splices include surrogate-pair insertion and deletion with reference parity.

name: deleting_in_middle_of_multibyte_char_moves_the_cursor_to_after_the_character
rationale: Interior UTF-16 cursors and their resolved positions are compared directly with Rust.

name: splice_text
rationale: Random and deterministic UTF-16 splices are checked after every operation against Rust.

name: cursors
rationale: Live and deleted cursor targets are compared with the UTF-16 Rust reference.

name: mark
rationale: Go and Rust independently author the same mark and cross-load the resulting marked text.

name: unmark
rationale: Go and Rust independently unmark an interior UTF-16 range and cross-load the split spans.

name: save_with_empty_commits
rationale: Sequences of empty changes save, load in Rust, preserve metadata, and retain their head hashes.

name: get_changes_with_hash_of_empty_change_produces_correct_result
rationale: ChangesSince returns the empty change from no heads and no changes when given its hash.

name: save_and_restore_empty
rationale: An empty native document saves and loads in Rust with no heads.

name: should allow a subset of changes to be sent
rationale: After acknowledging the initial frontier, only the subsequent change is sent.

name: should not generate messages once synced
rationale: The shared sync helper requires bounded quiescence and generation blocks while awaiting acknowledgement.

name: should allow simultaneous messages during synchronization
rationale: Native and official peers exchange edits created while another message is in flight.

name: should work with prior sync state
rationale: Quiescent and in-flight serialized sync sessions resume and converge.

name: should handle changes concurrent to the last sync heads
rationale: Both peers edit from the last shared frontier before each randomized sync round.

name: should sync three nodes
rationale: Three native/reference peers relay and converge concurrent changes.

name: should support unicode when creating text
rationale: Emoji-bearing text documents load in both JavaScript-to-Go and Go-to-JavaScript directions.

name: should handle multi character grapheme clusters
rationale: Random UTF-16 operations include non-ASCII and surrogate pairs with Rust parity.

name: should support insertion
rationale: Random insertion positions are checked against the official reference after every operation.

name: should support deletion
rationale: Random UTF-16 deletions are checked against the official reference after every operation.

name: should handle concurrent insertion
rationale: Both engines insert concurrently at randomized positions and compare values and heads.

name: getCursorPosition should work
rationale: Cursor bytes and resolved positions are compared directly with Rust.

name: should use javascript string indices
rationale: Cursor behavior at every relevant UTF-16 boundary of an emoji string matches Rust's JavaScript indexing mode.

name: should allow for usage of start/end cursors
rationale: Start and end cursor bytes and resolved UTF-16 positions match Rust.

name: should allow for usage of move before/after
rationale: Before/after movement bytes and deleted-target resolution are compared directly with Rust.

name: should convert negative indices into a start cursor
rationale: Negative Go cursor indices clamp to the canonical start cursor and match Rust.

name: should convert indices >= string length into an end cursor
rationale: Indices at and beyond UTF-16 text length clamp to the canonical end cursor.

name: can use cursors in common text operations
rationale: A stable cursor is resolved and used for replacement in native and Rust texts.

name: can use cursors in splice calls
rationale: Cursor-addressed UTF-16 splice operations produce identical native and Rust text.

name: handle basic set and read on root object
rationale: Root scalar writes and reads execute against native and Rust engines and cross-load in both directions.

name: handle overwrites to values
rationale: Multiple assignments in one change resolve to the final value in both engines.

name: it should be able to handle ints and floats at their limits
rationale: The scalar differential includes maximum unsigned integers, minimum signed integers, infinity, and NaN with bit-exact float comparison.

name: negative_64
rationale: The minimum signed 64-bit scalar round-trips through native, Rust, and native-to-Rust loading.

name: save_and_reload_create_object
rationale: A list created without children is saved, loaded, mutated under a new actor, saved again, and read by Rust.

name: handle set with object value
rationale: Nested map values are authored independently by Go and Rust and cross-loaded.

name: handle simple list creation
rationale: An empty list is created, committed, saved, loaded, and resolved as the same object.

name: handle simple lists
rationale: List insertion, indexed reads, replacement, deletion, change encoding, and cross-engine application are exercised.

name: test_local_inc_in_map
rationale: Map counters are incremented repeatedly with positive and negative deltas in native and Rust engines.

name: save_and_load_incremented_counter
rationale: Incremented counters are saved by Go, loaded by Rust, and compared after concurrent merging.

name: add_concurrent_increments_of_same_property
rationale: Two actors increment the same counter concurrently; Go merges to the summed value and Rust verifies it.

name: increment_non_counter_map
rationale: Both native and Rust reject incrementing an integer map property.

name: increment_non_counter_list
rationale: Both native and Rust reject incrementing an integer list element.

name: should add concurrent increments of the same property
rationale: Concurrent increments merge additively and are loaded by the JavaScript-compatible Rust engine.

name: should allow deleting counters from maps
rationale: Native and Rust both delete a map counter after it is committed.

name: should initially be an empty map
rationale: Fresh native and Rust root maps expose no keys.

name: should save and load maps with @ symbols in the keys
rationale: Empty, lexical, and @-containing keys persist through native and Rust save/load.

name: should allow a document to be cloned
rationale: Native and Rust forks preserve base history while accepting independent changes.

name: should allow passing an actorId when instantiating from an existing object
rationale: Fork assigns the requested actor before creating and merging independent changes.

name: missing_actors_when_docs_are_forked
rationale: Forked histories with a new actor save, merge, and resolve in both native and Rust engines.

name: have many list methods
rationale: Randomized indexed insertion, replacement, and deletion execute identically and produce identical change hashes in Go and Rust.

name: list_deletion
rationale: Random list histories repeatedly delete first, middle, and last elements and compare every remaining value with Rust.

name: handle basic sets over many changes
rationale: One thousand randomized nested-map changes produce identical values and change hashes in Go and Rust.

name: delete_only_change
rationale: Random histories commit standalone map deletions and compare their hashes and resulting absence with Rust.

name: allows_empty_keys_in_mappings
rationale: The randomized map key set explicitly includes the empty string for writes, reads, overwrites, and deletion.

name: test_merging_test_conflicts_then_saving_and_loading
rationale: Concurrent map assignments are merged, all conflicts and the winner are checked, then the merged document is loaded by Rust.

name: repeated_map_assignment_which_resolves_conflict_not_ignored
rationale: A merged two-value conflict is overwritten and verified to contain exactly the resolving value.

name: test_overwriting_a_conflict
rationale: The winner and both conflicts are checked before a new assignment clears the conflict.

name: no_conflict_on_repeated_assignment
rationale: Repeated assignments in one change produce exactly one visible value in Go and Rust.

name: handle text
rationale: The same text creation, UTF-16 splice, save, cross-load, and materialization scenario runs independently in Go, Rust, and JavaScript.

name: should generate a hash
rationale: All engines generate heads, and transferred Go changes retain their original hash through JavaScript.

name: should default to current timestamp
rationale: CommitNow records a current Unix-seconds timestamp in native and Rust changes.

name: should allow user provided timestamp
rationale: An explicit timestamp is decoded unchanged from native and Rust changes.

name: should allow no timestamp
rationale: A zero time records the protocol no-timestamp value in native and Rust changes.

name: should default to current timestamp
rationale: EmptyCommitNow records a current Unix-seconds timestamp in native and Rust changes.

name: should allow user provided timestamp
rationale: An explicit timestamp is preserved on empty native and Rust changes.

name: should allow no timestamp
rationale: Zero-timestamp empty changes decode and round-trip with JavaScript and Rust.

name: should be the same as saveIncremental since heads of the last saveIncremental
rationale: Repeated incremental saves emit only new changes, and a full save advances the incremental cursor.

name: should allow you to load incrementally
rationale: Native and Rust incrementally load each other's changes, ignore duplicates, and converge heads.

name: should incrementally apply changes since the last given version
rationale: Two successive incremental batches apply in both Go-to-Rust and Rust-to-Go directions.

name: should return true if the document in question has all the heads
rationale: Native and Rust report true for current, historical, and empty head sets.

name: should return false if the document does not have the heads
rationale: Native and Rust report false for an unknown change hash.

name: should return the document at its correct heads
rationale: Historical scalar and text values are materialized at the first head after later changes exist.

name: should report missing dependencies with out-of-order applyChanges
rationale: A child-first change is queued, reports only its missing parent, then clears the dependency after the parent arrives.

name: should clear conflicts after assigning a new value
rationale: A two-actor conflict is resolved by assignment and GetAll returns one value.

name: should not register any conflicts on repeated assignment
rationale: Repeated writes from one actor retain only the final scalar value.

name: should not ignore field updates that resolve a conflict
rationale: The conflict-resolving map update is committed and remains the sole value.

name: get change metadata
rationale: Go validates the actor, sequence, start operation, timestamp, message, dependencies, operations, and hash of an official change.

name: should return a decoded representation of the change
rationale: Every operation and metadata field in a JavaScript change is decoded and asserted before byte-compatible re-encoding.

name: test_get_change_meta
rationale: The native decoder exposes and verifies the official change metadata fields and hash.

name: test_get_last_local_change_generation
rationale: The most recent generated change is returned with its exact hash and bytes and preserved by JavaScript.

name: test_compressed_changes
rationale: An official change is compressed, decoded, and verified to preserve its original hash and change type.

name: overlong_leb
rationale: The native reader rejects an overlong, non-minimal unsigned LEB128 representation.

name: zero_length_data
rationale: Empty input is a deterministic loader regression seed and part of the native decoder fuzz corpus.

name: fuzz_crashers
rationale: Every pinned upstream fuzz crasher is a deterministic test and fuzz seed for the native decoder.

name: load
rationale: Ordered, compressed, and out-of-order official multi-change fixtures all load successfully.

name: obj_id_64bits
rationale: Official change and document fixtures with a 2^42 object operation ID either reject safely or preserve the full ID.

name: ops_on_wrong_objets
rationale: Map writes on list/text objects and sequence writes on maps reject consistently with Rust.

name: load_doc_with_deleted_objects
rationale: Deleted list, text, map, and table objects save and load in native and Rust engines with an empty root.

name: insert_after_many_deletes
rationale: One hundred map insert/delete pairs commit and materialize without index corruption in Go or Rust.

name: merge_after_noop_then_real_put
rationale: A fork records a no-op change followed by a real assignment, then merges and reloads in Go and Rust.

name: merge_panic_after_putting_value_equal_to_initial_value
rationale: An equal-value assignment creates no operation and does not panic when merged with a real fork update.

name: load_incremental_with_corrupted_tail
rationale: Native and Rust apply the complete valid prefix and ignore the corrupt trailing fragment.

name: test_load_incremental_partial_load
rationale: A standalone incremental change batch applies to a peer in both Go-to-Rust and Rust-to-Go directions.

name: read_only_sync_does_not_apply_incoming_changes
rationale: Native and Rust read-only receivers reject incoming changes in both engine directions.

name: read_only_empty_peer_syncs_with_data_peer
rationale: An empty read-only peer exchanges protocol state with a populated peer without applying its document.

name: changes_not_sent_to_read_only_peer
rationale: The publisher discovers read-only mode and quiesces without repeatedly sending document changes.

name: peer_discovers_remote_read_only_status
rationale: PeerReadOnly is asserted after flag exchange for native and Rust publishers.

name: switch_read_only_to_read_write_mid_session
rationale: A read-only peer switches to read-write, requests a reset, receives prior changes, and converges.

name: generate_message_after_set_read_only_even_with_in_flight
rationale: Changing to read-only forces a new message while an earlier message remains in flight.

name: generate_message_after_set_read_only_false_even_with_in_flight
rationale: Changing back to read-write forces a reset message despite an in-flight message.

name: both_peers_read_only
rationale: Two peers with independent changes enter read-only mode and exchange no document changes.

name: both_peers_read_only_converges_to_none
rationale: Both read-only peers quiesce while retaining distinct local heads.

name: both_read_only_both_make_local_changes
rationale: Both peers begin with independent local changes that remain isolated during read-only synchronization.

name: both_toggle_read_only_to_read_write_simultaneously
rationale: Both peers switch to read-write simultaneously and converge their prior local changes.

name: both_toggle_read_only_to_read_write_with_new_changes
rationale: Independent changes created before the simultaneous transition are exchanged after reset.

name: should not apply incoming changes when read-only
rationale: Read-only behavior is tested in both native-to-Rust and Rust-to-native directions.

name: should discover peer read-only status
rationale: Both implementations expose the remote read-only state after flags are exchanged.

name: should allow switching from read-only to read-write
rationale: One-sided and simultaneous read-only transitions reset and converge against Rust.

name: should do unicode sensibly
rationale: An emoji-range mark followed by a UTF-16 prefix insertion materializes identically in Go and JavaScript.

name: can split a block
rationale: Go and Rust independently insert and populate block marker maps at matching rich-text positions.

name: can join a block
rationale: Go and Rust delete a block marker, preserve surrounding text, and cross-load identical spans.

name: unmark_part_of_range
rationale: Unmarking the middle of a marked range produces two marked outer spans and an unmarked gap.

name: unmark_creates_gaps
rationale: Null mark operations remove the mark from the requested interior range without affecting adjacent spans.

name: mark_splits
rationale: A single mark split by unmarking materializes as separate marked spans.

name: different_adjacent_marks
rationale: Different marks on adjacent ranges remain separate at head and element anchors.

name: marks_on_emoji
rationale: Marked emoji ranges and subsequent UTF-16 edits materialize with Rust parity.

name: merge_concurrent_map_prop_updates
rationale: Twenty deterministic multi-change histories update shared map properties concurrently and compare every conflict with an independently merged Rust history.

name: concurrent_updates_of_same_field
rationale: Both actors repeatedly assign the same bounded key set before merge-order and Rust differential checks.

name: concurrent_updates_of_same_list_element
rationale: Both actors replace shared base-list elements in deterministic randomized histories and compare the merged sequence with Rust.

name: concurrent_insertions_at_different_list_positions
rationale: Independent actors insert throughout the same base list and both merge orders are compared with Rust.

name: concurrent_insertions_at_same_list_position
rationale: The bounded random index space repeatedly creates same-position concurrent insertions and verifies deterministic Rust ordering.

name: concurrent_assignment_and_deletion_of_a_map_entry
rationale: Each actor independently assigns and deletes the same bounded key set before conflict comparison with Rust.

name: concurrent_assignment_and_deletion_of_list_entry
rationale: Concurrent list replacements and deletions are merged in both orders and compared element-by-element with Rust.

name: it should handle conflicts the same in merges as with loads
rationale: Native and Rust independently construct and merge identical histories, then compare all scalar conflicts.

name: should obtain the same conflicts, regardless of merge order
rationale: Left-first and right-first merges converge to identical conflicts in native and Rust engines.

name: does_not_interleave_sequence_insertions_at_same_position
rationale: Two multi-value insertions at the same position remain contiguous and match Rust ordering.

name: mutliple_insertions_at_same_list_position_with_insertion_by_greater_actor_id
rationale: The greater actor's insertion chunk is ordered before the lesser actor's chunk in Go and Rust.

name: mutliple_insertions_at_same_list_position_with_insertion_by_lesser_actor_id
rationale: Actor-order-independent construction converges to the same chunk ordering in Go and Rust.

name: insertion_after_a_deleted_list_element
rationale: An insertion anchored after an element deleted concurrently remains visible in the correct position.

name: should not interleave sequence insertions at the same position
rationale: Concurrent insertion chunks remain contiguous with native and Rust parity.

name: should handle insertion by greater actor ID
rationale: Explicit deterministic actors verify greater-ID insertion ordering.

name: should handle insertion by lesser actor ID
rationale: Explicit deterministic actors verify lesser-ID insertion ordering.

name: should handle insertion after a deleted list element
rationale: Delete/insert concurrency preserves the insertion anchored to a deleted element.

name: rollback_with_no_ops
rationale: Rollback with no pending operations returns zero in native and Rust engines.

name: it should be able to roll back a transaction
rationale: Pending scalar and object operations are rolled back, committed values and heads remain unchanged, and Rust reports the same cancelled operation count.

name: repeated_list_assignment_which_resolves_conflict_not_ignored
rationale: A list element is assigned across a merge and then reassigned; both engines resolve to the single winning value and agree on heads.

name: add_increments_only_to_preceeded_values
rationale: Two actors create and increment separate counters at the same key; the increments stay attached to their own counters, yielding conflicting values 1 and 3 on both engines.

name: assignment_conflicts_of_different_types
rationale: Three actors assign a string, a list, and a map to the same key; both engines pick the same winner and produce identical heads.

name: changes_within_conflicting_map_field
rationale: A string and a populated map conflict at one key; both engines expose the winning map with its inner value and agree on heads.

name: changes_within_conflicting_list_element
rationale: Two actors replace the same list element with maps and mutate them across merges; both engines expose the same winning map contents and heads.

name: concurrently_assigned_nested_maps_should_not_merge
rationale: Two actors assign different maps to the same key; the maps do not merge and the winning map keeps exactly one key on both engines.

name: concurrent_deletion_of_same_list_element
rationale: Both actors delete the same list element concurrently; the element is removed once and the surviving order matches on both engines.

name: concurrent_updates_at_different_levels
rationale: One actor edits a nested map while another deletes it; the deletion wins and only the sibling list remains on both engines.

name: concurrent_updates_of_concurrently_deleted_objects
rationale: One actor updates a nested object another actor deleted concurrently; the deletion wins and the parent becomes empty on both engines.

name: insertion_consistent_with_causality
rationale: Interleaved head insertions across repeated merges produce the causally ordered list one,two,three,four on both engines.

name: save_restore_complex1
rationale: A todo list with a conflicting title survives save and reload; both engines expose both conflicting titles and the retained boolean.

name: save_restore_complex_transactional
rationale: The transactional variant groups writes into single commits; the reloaded document exposes the same conflicting titles and boolean on both engines.

name: big_list
rationale: A list of many null elements is replaced with map objects; both engines materialize N+1 maps that survive a cross-engine save/load with identical heads.

name: invalid_index
rationale: Inserting or putting beyond the end of a list is rejected by both engines while an in-bounds put succeeds.

name: has_our_changes
rationale: Two peers with concurrent changes synchronize until each contains the other's change and both converge to identical heads on both engines.

name: make_sure_load_incremental_doesnt_skip_a_load_with_a_common_head
rationale: Incremental loads that share a common head are not skipped; both engines end with the expected merged two-head frontier.
